title: Check the 451-factor finite schedule against the live balanced receiver
body:
The installed #7914 six-stage ternary receiver has different factor count, cutoff, carrier and precision requirements from the recorded #7863 451-factor schedule. The new receipt also binds a labelled paid contact and two different helper floor roles.

## Scope and source

Pins #7914 and #7863. The six-stage peer cap ends 7.814e−12 below the candidate consumer rate; a q=3 receiver does not satisfy the candidate’s stated large-prime sufficient cover. The source comparator is #7830 at `87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15`. Base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`; toolkit #7852 `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`. The included source manifest identifies every public dependency used.

## Reproduction

Extract `research/p104-stock451-physical-interface/replay.tar.gz` into an empty directory, check its checksum manifest, and run the extracted commands. A clean-copy verifier checked the pinned source blobs, exact 451 path tags, cutoff arithmetic and deliberate source and owner mutations. Hosted execution is separate.

## Open next questions

Prove a new 451 ternary cover or supply a suitable q-prime receiver, then replay the actual integer-product recovery path.

Clear1nsight prepared this result with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit DreamingOfClouds for the P104 toolkit and the predecessor authors identified in the archive. [Campaign board](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/7111#discussioncomment-19789228).
